back: A financial plan for a future period, in money or units, of expected income, spending or output.
Sales (units and revenue), production (units to make), purchases (materials to buy), cash (inflows, outflows, balances).
Units to produce = planned sales + planned closing inventory − opening inventory.
The difference between a budgeted figure and the actual figure.
Favourable: revenue above budget or costs below budget. Adverse: revenue below budget or costs above budget.
Planning, control, targets and motivation, coordination of departments, support when raising finance.
Based on forecasts that may be wrong; time-consuming; inflexible; unrealistic targets demotivate.
The person responsible for keeping to a particular budget.
